items.title: The Irreplaceable Role of Cash in Times of Crisis
items.summary: Article published by the European Central Bank (ECB) analysing how demand for euro cash surges in times of uncertainty, specifically during major recent crises —the 2008 financial crisis, the 2014-15 sovereign debt crisis in Greece, the COVID-19 pandemic, Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and the Iberian blackout of April 2025. The study highlights that the unique attributes of cash —its tangible, resilient, offline nature (i.e. independent of networks, electricity, telecommunications or external authorisations) and its wide acceptance— make it both a safe-haven asset and an essential payment instrument in times of crisis. For these reasons, several European and national authorities (including the governments of the Netherlands, Austria and Finland) have issued recommendations to the general public to keep some cash reserves in case of sudden and unexpected contingencies.
